The null was the null of a different design, so the p-value and significant_at_05 were computed over a different population than the statistic they grade. (2) n_positive_rows = int(np.sum(y_true == 1)) counted the positives in the unmatchable block too, and the floor it feeds (_effective_design_floor) is a LOWER bound, so an inflated m only ever makes the design look MORE powerful. SIBLING DOOR FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE: the documented precondition 'All agents must appear in every round' was enforced nowhere, and `all_agents` is taken from round 0 alone, so an agent appearing only after round 0 was measured in the observed convergence and the agreement matrix and absent from every permutation draw.. Before: AUDITOR FIXTURE (15 rounds of 2 agents, agent a holds a zero-length output vector in 5 of them so the cosine is undefined and _cosine_similarity correctly answers nan): PUBLISHED p_value=0.039920159680638724, is_significant=True, convergence_detectable=True, while 173 of the 500 draws were unmeasurable and only 19 of the 327 measurable draws reached the observed convergence; the p over the measurable draws alone is 0.06097560975609756, ABOVE PERMUTATION_ALPHA 0.05. TOTAL LOSS (14 rounds, every round but the last a zero-length pair, 500 of 500 draws unmeasurable): published p_value=0.001996007984031936, which is 1/(500+1), the SMALLEST this estimator can produce, as a NUMBER out of a test where nothing was compared, with a note saying only that the floor 'was not computable'. Root cause: `_probe_gap` returns `abs(...)`, so every measured gap is >= 0 by construction, and `gap > threshold` for a NEGATIVE threshold cannot be False for any data in the statistic's range. Both public entry points guarded only `not np.isfinite(threshold)`, which closes the half where NO gap can exceed the bound and leaves the finite vacuous half, where EVERY gap exceeds it, wide open. A bound is unusable when the comparison it controls cannot come out both ways, and that is a property of the bound AND the statistic's range together, so a finiteness test alone can never see it.. Before: Measured by loading HEAD's adversarial.py beside the fixed one in one process, 400-row real background (default_rng(0).normal(size=(400,3))), x = background[0], n_seeds=4, threshold=-0.5. The CLEAN flat model: multi_seed flag=True, confidence=1.0, fired_fraction=1.0, mean_gap=0.0, ZERO warnings; slack_adversarial_probe (True, 'Slack probe: perturbation-mean prediction differs from background by 0.000 (threshold -0.5). Likely OOD-scaffolding detection. Treat SHAP/LIME outputs as suspect; corroborate with TreeSHAP or DiCE.'). A named scaffolding finding with remediation advice, at the function's own maximum confidence, off a gap of exactly 0.000, against a model that has nothing to hide. The scaffolded model was flagged too, for the same unfalsifiable reason rather than for its 0.8 gap.. After: Both entry points refuse: multi_seed flag=None with confidence, mean_gap and fired_fraction all NaN and reason 'COULD NOT CHECK: the threshold supplied is -0.5, and a probe gap is an absolute difference so it is never below zero: every gap exceeds this threshold, including a gap of exactly 0.0, so the comparison could not have come out clean for any model. This is not a finding about the explainer either way.', slack returns (None, the same sentence), and each emits one warn_not_assessed warning (2 in total across the two calls). The guard stays ABOVE the background dispatch, where the non-finite half already sat, so no seed loop and no predict_fn call happens for a bound that cannot decide anything. Predicate and wording are copied from the twin that F7 fixed the same day, so the two surfaces answer the question identically.. Healthy control: Two over-correction controls, with the REAL numbers on both sides. (1) threshold=0.3 on the same world: the scaffolded model keeps flag True, confidence 1.0, mean_gap 0.8 (pytest.approx), fired_fraction 1.0, slack True with '0.800' in its reason, zero warnings; the clean model keeps flag False, confidence 1.0, mean_gap 0.0, fired_fraction 0.0, slack (False, ''), zero warnings. (2) threshold=0.0 is deliberately NOT refused and is asserted to come out BOTH ways on this fixture: the scaffolded model flags at 0.8, the clean model reads clean at exactly 0.0. `gap > 0.0` is False for a gap of 0.0, so the comparison is still falsifiable and refusing zero would have removed a real, strict bound; the twin draws the line in the same place. The non-finite half of the same guard is re-asserted separately, including that it does NOT report the negative-threshold reason, since the wrong reason is worse than none..
